report_data.executive_summary:
The assessment record documents four beneficiary-class weighings under 11 CCR § 7152(a); each records that the benefits outweigh the identified negative impacts, with every harm pathway covered by an implemented and tested safeguard leaving a low residual exposure. **How Sierra Outfitters, Inc. processes personal information for Store-financing eligibility screening.**

Sierra Outfitters, Inc. collects Contact identifiers (name, email, phone), Financial information, Employment information, and Other from the applicant, from Experian under a reseller agreement, and from the fraud-consortium database operated by Sentinel Risk LLC.

The activity assessed in this Risk Assessment is Store-financing eligibility screening, undertaken for the purpose of deciding store-financing applications within minutes at point of sale while screening for identity fraud. The analysis that follows — scope, processing, benefits, negative impacts, safeguards, and the weighing conclusion — is directed to that activity.

On the record as documented, one activity requiring assessment was assessed for this Risk Assessment. For Store-financing eligibility screening, every identified negative impact is addressed by a recorded safeguard leaving a low residual exposure; the weighing across all four beneficiary classes records that the benefits outweigh the identified negative impacts. One documentation element — the dated initiation decision under 11 CCR § 7152(a)(7) — remains to be recorded by the accountable business owner before the assessment closes.

The record before this assessment is complete: every question the intake asks has been answered. What follows carries an action plan of 1 item — 0 preconditions to be completed before processing begins, and the remainder scheduled after launch.

report_data.submission_summary:
[§ 7157 submission / § 7155 retention] Under 11 CCR § 7157(a)(1), for risk assessments conducted in 2026 and 2027, a business must submit to the Agency the information required by § 7157(b) no later than April 1, 2028. Under § 7157(a)(2), for risk assessments conducted after 2027, that information is due no later than April 1 following any year during which the business conducted the risk assessments — for assessments conducted in 2028, no later than April 1, 2029. Under § 7155(c), a business must retain its risk assessments, including original and updated versions, for as long as the processing continues or for five years after the completion of the risk assessment, whichever is later. Under § 7155(a)(2)-(3), at least once every three years a business must review, and update as necessary, its risk assessments; and notwithstanding that cadence, it must update a risk assessment whenever there is a material change relating to the processing activity, as soon as feasibly possible but no later than 45 calendar days from the date of the material change. A change is material if it creates new negative impacts, increases the magnitude or likelihood of previously identified negative impacts under § 7152(a)(5), or diminishes the effectiveness of the safeguards under § 7152(a)(6). The customer, in consultation with qualified legal counsel, determines the submission window that applies to this assessment and calendars the corresponding review and update dates.

Separately, the cybersecurity-audit obligation under 11 CCR § 7121(a) phases in as follows:

[§ 7121(a) phase-in schedule] Under 11 CCR § 7121(a), a business must complete its first cybersecurity audit report no later than one of three cohort deadlines fixed by the regulation: — Per § 7121(a)(1), April 1, 2028, if the business's annual gross revenue for 2026 was more than one hundred million dollars ($100,000,000) as of January 1, 2027; the audit would cover the period from January 1, 2027, through January 1, 2028. — Per § 7121(a)(2), April 1, 2029, if the business's annual gross revenue for 2027 was between fifty million dollars ($50,000,000) and one hundred million dollars ($100,000,000) as of January 1, 2028; the audit would cover the period from January 1, 2028, through January 1, 2029. — Per § 7121(a)(3), April 1, 2030, if the business's annual gross revenue for 2028 was less than fifty million dollars ($50,000,000); the audit would cover the period from January 1, 2029, through January 1, 2030. The customer, in consultation with qualified legal counsel, determines which tier its revenue places it in and calendars the corresponding deadline.

[§ 7121(a) cohort on the recorded band] On the recorded annual gross revenue band (Over $100M), the § 7121(a)(1) cohort deadline is April 1, 2028, covering the audit period January 1, 2027, through January 1, 2028. The customer, in consultation with qualified legal counsel, confirms this cohort against its final revenue figures.

Submission postures under 11 CCR § 7120(b):

§ 7120(b)(1) incorporates Civil Code § 1798.140(d)(1)(C), which applies when a business "Derives 50 percent or more of its annual revenues from selling or sharing consumers’ personal information". On the current record this threshold is not met.

§ 7120(b)(2)(A) applies when a business "Processed the personal information of 250,000 or more consumers or households in the preceding calendar year". On the current record this threshold is not met.

§ 7120(b)(2)(B) applies when a business "Processed the sensitive personal information of 50,000 or more consumers in the preceding calendar year". On the current record this threshold is met.

processing_narrative:
**How Sierra Outfitters, Inc. processes personal information for Store-financing eligibility screening.**

Sierra Outfitters, Inc. collects Contact identifiers (name, email, phone), Financial information, Employment information, and Other from the applicant, from Experian under a reseller agreement, and from the fraud-consortium database operated by Sentinel Risk LLC. The information is used Assess creditworthiness and verify identity for store-financing applications so qualified customers can finance purchases at the point of sale. Sierra Outfitters, Inc. discloses this information to Experian (credit bureau, reseller agreement); Sentinel Risk LLC (fraud consortium, service-provider addendum); CoreLedger Inc. (loan-servicing platform, service-provider addendum). All three under CCPA service-provider contracts prohibiting secondary use. through Notice at Collection and Privacy policy. The record sets a retention period of 25 months from decision, applying the criterion that Fixed period from collection. At the end of that period the information is handled under the record's stated deletion process: Automated deletion with confirmation.

risk_assessment_by_activity: The assessment record documents four beneficiary-class weighings under 11 CCR § 7152(a); each records that the benefits outweigh the identified negative impacts. Every harm pathway carries a recorded safeguard with a low residual band. The dated initiation decision under 11 CCR § 7152(a)(7) is reserved to the accountable business owner and must be recorded before the assessment closes.

The record states that Sierra Outfitters, Inc. considered less-intrusive alternatives as follows: Only the fields on the credit application and the bureau report are processed: identity, income, tenure, and account references. Browsing history, purchase history outside the financed order, and marketing profiles are excluded by design. Under 11 CCR § 7152(a)(2), this record is the operative statement for the balancing frame.
